name: MCP2562
full_name: Microchip MCP2562 High-Speed CAN Transceiver with Split VIO Supply
description: The MCP2562 is Microchip's second-generation high-speed CAN physical-layer transceiver, interfacing a CAN protocol controller to the two-wire differential bus. It is a PHY only: it carries no protocol logic and must be driven by a controller such as the MCP2515 or an MCU's CAN peripheral. It runs the bus side from a 5 V VDD (1 Mb/s, ISO 11898-2/-5), with extensive fault protection - TXD and bus permanent-dominant detection, short-circuit and high-voltage automotive transient protection, thermal shutdown, and bus pins that disconnect when unpowered so a dead node never loads the bus. Its standout trait is the separate VIO supply pin (pin 5): tie VIO to a 3.3 V (or down to 1.8 V) rail and the TXD/RXD logic levels track that rail, letting it interface a 3.3 V MCU directly without external level shifters - the key difference from its sibling the MCP2561, which instead exposes a SPLIT common-mode pin there.

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: Transmit data input from the CAN controller (LOW = dominant). Logic threshold referenced to VIO.

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: Receive data output to the CAN controller. Output level referenced to VIO (down to 1.8 V).

pins.name: VIO
pins.description: Logic-side I/O supply reference; tie to the MCU's I/O rail (1.8 V to 5.5 V) so TXD/RXD swing matches, enabling direct 3.3 V interfacing. (On the MCP2561 this pin is SPLIT instead.)

pins.name: STBY
pins.description: Standby mode control; high level puts the device in low-current standby, low level enables normal operation.

extra.supply: 5 V VDD plus separate VIO logic supply
extra.fault_protection: TXD and bus permanent-dominant detection, short-circuit, automotive HV transient, thermal shutdown, POR/brown-out on VDD
extra.unpowered_bus: bus pins disconnect when unpowered (no bus loading)
extra.system_voltage: suitable for 12 V and 24 V systems

typical_application: Mixed-voltage CAN node: a 3.3 V MCU CAN controller (or MCP2515) drives TXD/RXD with VIO tied to the MCU's 3.3 V rail, while VDD runs the 5 V bus side into a 120-ohm-terminated twisted pair.
gotchas: Transceiver (PHY) only - pair with an MCP2515 or MCU CAN controller; it does not frame messages.
VIO (pin 5) must be powered - tie it to the logic rail (commonly 3.3 V); leaving it unconnected breaks the digital interface. This is the pin that differs from the MCP2561 (SPLIT).
VDD undervoltage threshold is ~4 V and VIO ~1.2 V - both supplies must be valid before the transceiver enables.
STBY (pin 8) must be driven low for normal operation; high selects standby.
Bus still requires external 120-ohm termination at both ends.
